round1_person_reads.sentence: The question is whether programmes meant to improve education for children and young people with disabilities in low- and middle-income countries work, and which kinds work best.
We drew on four documents, each held in full text: the 2025 systematic review, the 2018 rapid evidence assessment, the 2022 educational technology review and the 2020 evidence and gap map.

We read the 2025 review's abstract, plain-language summary, discussion and conclusions, and the 2018 assessment's executive summary and conclusions; we did not read the individual studies the reviews include.
We did not obtain a 2020 correction to the evidence and gap map, because its publisher's terms do not allow our tools to read it.
We did not search databases systematically; these documents came from a web search on 29 October 2026.
Findings in our sources we judged outside this question

Judged not material to this question: “Investing in interventions to improve well‐being of people with disabilities will be critical to achieving the 2030 agenda for sustainable development goals.” (Evidence and gap map of studies assessing the effectiveness ); it states a policy goal, not a finding about whether these programmes work.

Judged not material to this question: “The EGM summarized here provides a starting point for researchers, decision makers and programme managers to access the available research evidence on the effectiveness of …” (Evidence and gap map of studies assessing the effectiveness ); it describes what the map is for, not a finding about whether these programmes work.

round1_person_reads.sentence: The question is what part removing carbon dioxide from the air can play, alongside cutting emissions, in reaching net zero, now and in the decades ahead.

We hold four documents in full and drew on all four: the Summary for Policymakers and Chapter 12 of the IPCC's 2022 Working Group III report, the Summary for Policymakers of the IPCC's 2021 Working Group I report, and the 2026 third edition of The State of Carbon Dioxide Removal.
We did not read the other chapters of the IPCC reports or the primary studies these assessments draw on, and we did not search for studies of individual removal methods.
Findings in our sources we judged outside this question
Judged not material to this question: “GHG emissions (GtCO2-eq yr –1) a.” (IPCC AR6 WGIII Summary for Policymakers); figure label text extracted with statement B.6.4, not a finding.
Judged not material to this question: “Global GHG emissions b …” (IPCC AR6 WGIII Summary for Policymakers); figure legend text extracted with statement B.6.4, not a finding.

Judged not material to this question: “C.3.4 In modelled pathways that reach global net zero GHG emissions, at the point they reach net zero GHG, around 74% [54 to 90%] of …” (IPCC AR6 WGIII Summary for Policymakers); it divides emission cuts by sector and says nothing of removal's part.

Outside this question: “CO2 capture and subsurface injection is a mature technology for gas processing and enhanced oil recovery.” (IPCC AR6 WGIII Summary for Policymakers); capture at fossil and industrial sources is not removal from the air.

Outside this question: “In contrast to the oil and gas sector, CCS is less mature in the power sector, as well as in cement and chemicals production, where …” (IPCC AR6 WGIII Summary for Policymakers); capture at fossil and industrial sources is not removal from the air.

Judged not material to this question: “A.4.4 The equilibrium climate sensitivity is an important quantity used to estimate how the climate responds to radiative …” (IPCC AR6 WGI Summary for Policymakers); it concerns climate sensitivity, not the part removal plays.
